ai-at-work.title: India’s MoEngage bets that the future of marketing is millions of AI agents
ai-at-work.excerpt: The all-cash deal gives MoEngage access to technology that assigns AI agents to individual customers.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: MoEngage just picked up technology that deploys individual AI agents for each customer through an all-cash acquisition. This matters because it signals that personalization at scale is shifting from clever algorithms to distributed AI doing one-to-one work, which changes how we think about customer engagement platforms and internal comms tools. Honestly, I've seen plenty of "one AI per person" pitches before, and the real test will be whether this actually reduces marketing noise or just creates a million tiny annoying bots.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic’s Claude Tag is learning your company, one Slack message at a time
ai-at-work.excerpt: Anthropic’s new Claude Tag brings an always-on AI teammate to Slack. But beyond productivity, the feature is a strategic play to capture organizational context, institutional knowledge, and enterprise
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic just released Claude Tag, an AI bot for Slack that learns your company's specific context, knowledge, and workflows as it processes your messages. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that these tools aren't just about doing tasks faster—they're about creating detailed profiles of how your organization actually works, which raises real questions about data governance and vendor lock-in. The honest truth is that every message Claude ingests becomes its training ground, so before you celebrate the productivity gains, you should probably have a serious chat with your security and legal teams about what you're actually trading away.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Fika Jobs just scored 4 million dollars to build an AI-powered video hiring platform that lets algorithms conduct initial interviews instead of actual humans. For digital workplace folks, this matters because if this scales, it could reshape how companies onboard talent and whether remote hiring becomes even more automated and impersonal. Look, AI doing first-pass screening isn't new, but turning it into a TikTok-style experience feels like we're one step closer to hiring people based on their best angles and lip-sync abilities rather than actual competence.

ai-at-work.title: Anthropic debuts Claude Tag, a more capable AI teammate that lives within Slack
ai-at-work.excerpt: Anthropic PBC today unveiled a new version of its chatbot Claude that lives inside Slack, where it operates like a virtual employee. It’s called Claude Tag, and it’s designed to work across entire org
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic released Claude Tag, an AI assistant that operates directly within Slack as a kind of virtual team member that can help multiple employees across projects. This matters because digital workplace leaders are now looking at AI not as a separate tool but as something embedded into the collaboration platforms where people already spend their time. Honestly, this is the move everyone's been waiting for, but let's see if organizations can resist the urge to replace humans with it before they've even figured out what it's supposed to do.

tools-tech.title: I replaced Google Search with DuckDuckGo and Perplexity - my results were noticeably better
tools-tech.excerpt: With Google now a cesspool of AI-generated answers, here's how to work smarter: DuckDuckGo and Perplexity are the best one-two punch in search today.
tools-tech.dwp_take: A tech writer ditched Google Search for DuckDuckGo and Perplexity, finding the results cleaner and more reliable as Google's search results get clogged with AI garbage. This matters because your workforce increasingly depends on search to find information, complete tasks, and make decisions, so a degraded search experience directly impacts productivity and information quality. Look, I've watched tool transitions for three decades, and when Google starts losing people over quality issues, that's significant, though good luck getting your IT department to approve a new search tool without three months of security reviews.

tools-tech.title: Meta pauses employee monitoring program after data protections fail
tools-tech.excerpt: An extensive program at Meta to gather a wide range of data from employees to train its AI model has been frozen after employees reportedly broke through its guardrails and accessed restricted data, a
tools-tech.dwp_take: Meta shut down an employee monitoring program designed to feed AI training data after workers repeatedly bypassed security controls meant to keep them out of restricted information. For digital workplace leaders, this is a textbook reminder that surveillance infrastructure requires rock-solid security architecture or it becomes liability theater. You can't build trust by watching your employees, and you definitely can't build it by doing so badly that they prove your systems don't work.

tools-tech.title: Robots will replace 700K delivery workers, warns head of e-commerce giant
tools-tech.excerpt: China’s e-commerce giant JD.com is preparing for a future where packages are delivered by robots instead of people. The company’s founder and chairman, Richard Liu, expects robots will “sooner or late
tools-tech.dwp_take: JD.com's founder says robots will eventually replace the company's 700,000 delivery workers, though he's expressed concern about their futures. This matters because it signals how seriously major employers view automation in logistics, and it raises real questions about how organizations plan for workforce transitions rather than just implementing technology. The irony is thick here: a leader simultaneously saying "robots are inevitable" and "I don't want people jobless" without actually committing to retraining programs shows exactly why workers should be skeptical when tech executives wring their hands about displacement.

tools-tech.title: Caught in the iCloud: Apple trial set in the UK

tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple is facing a UK class action lawsuit on behalf of 40 million iCloud users over alleged breaches of competition law, with potential damages hitting $3.9 billion. For digital workplace folks, this matters because it signals how regulators are increasingly willing to crack down on big tech's data practices and closed ecosystems, which directly affects how enterprises negotiate with these vendors. Here's the thing: when Apple loses cases like this, they don't suddenly become more open or user-friendly. They just get more expensive and more defensive, which is exactly the opposite of what your workplace needs.

digital-culture.title: Meta hits pause on tracking employee keystrokes to train AI after internal leak
digital-culture.excerpt: Just two months after Meta announced plans to track employee keystrokes and mouse movements to train its AI models, the company said it would pause the program after an alleged internal leak. Accordin
digital-culture.dwp_take: Meta announced it would pause a keystroke tracking program designed to feed AI training data after internal systems exposed employee private conversations and performance data. This matters because it's a textbook case of why surveillance initiatives need ironclad security architecture before deployment, not after you've already scared everyone. The real kicker is that Meta, of all companies, had to learn the hard way that employees won't volunteer their keystrokes for AI training if you can't even keep the data from leaking across your own network.

digital-culture.title: Feeling like you’re not enough can lead to burnout. These mindset shifts can prevent that
digital-culture.excerpt: Recently, I’ve had several conversations with high performers that follow a strikingly similar pattern. On paper, these people are the epitome of success: impressive titles, complex portfolios, and a
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece about high performers battling imposter syndrome and inadequacy feelings that drive them toward burnout. This matters because digital workplace leaders are managing increasingly distributed, isolated teams where you can't see when your best people are quietly drowning in self-doubt. Here's the thing though: no mindset shift solves a broken workload, and if your top performers feel like they're not enough, you might have a system problem masquerading as a psychology problem.

digital-culture.title: ‘The Big Short’ investor issues a dire warning about Nvidia. Here’s why he believes an ‘aggressive fall’ is coming, and how businesses can avoid the same fate
digital-culture.excerpt: Michael Burry, the investor whose controversial bet against the housing market was made famous in The Big Short, is continuing his campaign against another, perhaps even frothier target: Nvidia. Here’
digital-culture.dwp_take: Michael Burry is warning that Nvidia's stock is overvalued and headed for a significant correction, arguing the AI hype has gotten ahead of reality. Digital workplace leaders need to pay attention because many are making infrastructure and tool investments based on AI promises that might not deliver ROI if the bubble pops. After decades watching companies chase shiny tech trends, I'd say use Burry's warning as a reality check: vet your AI vendors hard and don't bet your budget on speculative tech just because everyone else is.

industry-news.title: Tata Electronics Leak Exposes 200,000 Files, Including Apple and Tesla Documents
industry-news.excerpt: Tata Electronics is investigating a cyber incident after leaked files reportedly included manufacturing documents for Apple and Tesla. The post Tata Electronics Leak Exposes 200,000 Files, Including A
industry-news.dwp_take: A Tata Electronics breach exposed 200,000 files containing sensitive manufacturing documents for major clients including Apple and Tesla. This matters because it shows that even massive suppliers to the world's biggest tech companies can't keep confidential data locked down, which means your organization's sensitive files are probably sitting in someone else's system with similar vulnerabilities. If you're still thinking your data is safe just because you hired an enterprise vendor, it's time to wake up and audit exactly where your information actually lives.

industry-news.title: Coupang’s $409M Fine Shows the Real Cost of Weak AI Governance
industry-news.excerpt: Recent AI and data security actions show why AI governance now belongs with boards, not just IT teams managing tools and access. The post Coupang’s $409M Fine Shows the Real Cost of Weak AI Governance
industry-news.dwp_take: Coupang got hit with a $409 million fine because their AI governance was basically a suggestion rather than a strategy. This matters because it proves that when your organization treats AI like just another tool that IT can handle in their spare time, regulators will absolutely make it your board's problem instead. After 30 years watching workplace tech, I can tell you that fining a company nearly half a billion dollars is a pretty expensive way to learn that governance belongs at the executive table, not buried in some IT ticketing system.

The real question isn't whether this works for Hollywood, it's whether your organization is ready for the creative chaos that happens when AI actually becomes useful at something people care about.
